solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fine liqueur, very exotic, enough for several shots at The Bull?

definitions.text: enough for several shots at The Bull?

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters are made into an unfamiliar new order

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker praises a fancy liqueur, strong enough to fuel several rounds of darts at a pub called The Bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bull' looks like a pub, but it is the bullseye of an archery target: a quiver holds arrows, so a full one supplies several shots at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiver is an archer's arrow case, so its full load is enough arrows for several shots at the target's centre.

clue.text: Land rating following maintenance of set standards

indicators.note: following says the sailor comes after the standards abbreviation

parts.note: QA, quality assurance, keeps work to set standards
a rating is an ordinary sailor, a tar

explanation.surface: A country's rating has followed its upkeep of agreed standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' is not a score but a naval rank: an ordinary seaman, or tar.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gulf state is a country, an example of a land.

clue.text: Flies driver away from edges of seismal epicentre, moving fast

indicators.note: moving means these letters shift into a new order
edges of means the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: taken as written
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A driver flees a quake zone at speed, away from the epicentre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges SL (the edges of 'seismal') with EPICENTRE to give INSECTREPEL; 'fast' adds LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray or cream that keeps bugs off drives flying pests away.

clue.text: Leave country house, heading off to get someone's goat?

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
to get someone's goat is to annoy them, to grate on them

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a country house, dashing off to steal a goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country house' looks like one phrase, but 'country' ends the definition. 'heading off' removes S from SEMI, a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's own country to settle in another.

clue.text: Pro's Glasgow abode that's an embarrassment!

parts.note: pro means for, giving FOR plus the S
hame is Scots for home

explanation.surface: A professional's house in Glasgow is a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' is not a professional but Latin for 'for'; HAME is the Scots form of home.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation reproaches someone for disgraceful conduct, so it says the thing is shameful.

clue.text: Added animation to story, cutting a dash

parts.note: lit, as in lit up, means brightened or enlivened

indicators.note: cutting means the letter A is removed from the story word

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A writer livened up a story by trimming a punctuation dash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dash' looks like the punctuation mark; 'a' is the letter cut from TALE, and 'dash' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash of something is a small amount, as in 'add a little milk'.

clue.text: First and foremost in nature you may perceive her?

definitions.text: First and foremost in nature you may perceive her?

indicators.note: first and foremost points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A poetic thought: wherever you look in the natural world, you might glimpse her presence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the initials of 'nature you may perceive her' spell the answer, and the sentence describes a spirit of nature.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth these are female spirits living in woods, rivers and hills, so nature is just where one might be glimpsed.

clue.text: Where Wellington is found touring island with German admiral

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the country's letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, NZ
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A German admiral goes on tour, visiting an island near Wellington.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester Nimitz was the US Pacific Fleet commander in the Second World War, of German descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimitz was a senior US Navy officer, the fleet admiral in the Pacific.

clue.text: Pleased, somehow, with a miserly "no comment"

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone pleased with themselves gives a stingy refusal to talk to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase declares the speaker will reveal nothing, the same as refusing comment.

clue.text: Den is Yankee appearing in sitcom briefly on Bravo in Spain

indicators.note: appearing in puts the letter for Yankee inside the shortened title
briefly means the sitcom title loses its last letter

parts.note: Hi-de-Hi! was a BBC sitcom set in a holiday camp
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ole is the Spanish cry of bravo

explanation.surface: A den has a Yank starring in a short sitcom, cheered on in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hi-de-Hi!' was a 1980s BBC holiday-camp sitcom. 'Bravo' looks like the radio code for B; here it is the cheer, Spanish OLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A den can be a secret hiding place or retreat.

clue.text: More attractive class of volunteers?

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force; 'of volunteers' gives the possessive TA'S
a tier is a level or class

explanation.surface: A question about which grade of unpaid helper is the more appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'class of volunteers' as the TA's tier: the Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasty is informal for appealing or attractive, so the comparative form means more attractive.

clue.text: Suddenly dropped bread basket, exhausted?

parts.note: bread basket is slang for the stomach, the tum
bled, as in bled dry, means drained or exhausted

explanation.surface: Someone fell all at once, dropping a bread basket, perhaps from exhaustion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread basket' is old slang for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: To tumble is to fall abruptly, so the past tense matches a sudden drop.

clue.text: Come back from Peru? Certainly, heading west

indicators.note: heading west says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the answer's letters are taken out of the words that follow, spanning their join

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A traveller is asked about returning from Peru and agrees, setting off westward.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'from' as a link; it signals the hiding. In an across answer westward means right to left, so the letters hidden in 'Peru? Certainly' are read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again or return, a straightforward synonym for coming back.

clue.text: Serious consequences of the boy's going to the Head, indeed!

parts.note: the boy is going to = he will, contracted to HE'LL
the top is the head of something
ay (aye) is an emphatic yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A lad is being sent to the headmaster's office, and there will be trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going to the Head' looks like a trip to the headteacher, but 'going to' belongs with 'the boy's' to make HE'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for severe trouble or retribution after some act means grave repercussions.

clue.text: What pre-euro Munich lived through is not progress!

definitions.meaning: before the euro, Germany used the Deutschmark, so Munich lived through the era of that currency
to stay in place while appearing busy, not advancing

explanation.surface: A wry note that German economic history before the single currency amounted to standing still.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is whimsical: the period when the Deutschmark was Germany's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching on the spot without moving forward is the idiom for failing to advance.

clue.text: Inexpert whiskey promotion Ireland stops

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the promotion and Ireland fill the whiskey

parts.note: malt is a malt whisky
an ad is a promotion
ROI is the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: Ireland halts an amateurish whiskey advertising campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whiskey' looks like the radio code for W; here it is the drink, MALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and lacking skill, the answer is a synonym for inexpert.

clue.text: Ring from Lima leaving greeting

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for Lima departs from the greeting word

parts.note: hallo is a variant of hello, a greeting
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone telephones from Lima, saying goodbye after a greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lima' looks like Peru's capital; it is the radio code word for L.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a circle of light, so it is a ring shape.

clue.text: State of light, mounted and switched on

indicators.note: mounted means climbing, so in a down answer the letters read upwards

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode
switched on is informal for alert, aware

explanation.surface: A lamp is put up and turned on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty US states, the first to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: President with trouble speaking's brought water

parts.note: John Adams was the second US president

indicators.note: speaking means the word for trouble is heard, not read

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A president with a speech problem has fetched some water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with trouble speaking' looks like a stammer; 'speaking' signals that AIL becomes its sound-alike ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam had only water to drink, so the jocular old phrase names plain drinking water.

clue.text: Nomad's extended round trip

parts.note: a lap is one circuit, a round trip of a track
extended means lengthened by one more letter, a second copy of the final one

explanation.surface: A wanderer's journey has been lengthened into a long round trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extended' doubles the last letter of the circuit word, adding another P.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sami people of northern Scandinavia were traditionally nomadic reindeer herders; this is the older name for one.

clue.text: Drop double-U in "watch"

parts.note: a bead is a drop of liquid, as of sweat

indicators.note: double says the word for U is written twice in a row

parts.note: U sounds like you, archaically YE

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a W into a word, as in a spelling puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double-U' looks like the letter W; it is 'you' twice, YE + YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a sharp, close eye on someone is to watch them closely and suspiciously.

clue.text: What's left on account: variable amount

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
Y is a variable, an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A bank statement shows what remains on account, a fluctuating sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is cricket: the on side of the field is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is what someone has left to others in a will.

clue.text: Stock at minimum price? That's a boost!

parts.note: to stock a shelf is to fill it
1P, one penny, is the smallest price in British money

explanation.surface: Buying shares at rock-bottom prices gives an investor a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: The I stands in for the figure 1, so 1P is one penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or lift that gives fresh energy.

clue.text: What's indulgently led to a live CD being remade

indicators.note: something remade is put together afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone led an indulgent life, and a live album was being re-recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led' belongs with the definition: the sweet life is what is led indulgently.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase for the sweet life describes a pleasurable, self-indulgent way of living.

clue.text: Girl's mother meeting the First Lady

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A girl's mother is introduced to the US president's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the First Lady' looks like the president's wife; here it is Eve, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Irish female first name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: About to pass on, looking up and down supplier?

indicators.note: looking up means reading upwards in a down answer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to pass on is to die

explanation.surface: A dying person is cheered up, then feels low again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is not low spirits but soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea duck's soft feathers are harvested for quilts, so it supplies down.

clue.text: Series of deliveries: each getting blanket

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
all can mean each, as in 'two all'

explanation.surface: Each item in a run of deliveries gets a blanket, as with a charitable parcel round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series of deliveries' is cricket: an over is six balls from one bowler. 'All' as in a score of 'two all' means each.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, blanket means comprehensive and covering everything, the same as total.

clue.text: Girl escorted outside I helped

indicators.note: outside says the girl and escort stand around the letter I

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
led means guided or escorted

explanation.surface: A girl was taken outside, and the speaker lent a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to be of use or benefit, so the past tense means assisted.

clue.text: Far from dear to the Scots, King Edward?

definitions.meaning: far from dear means cheap and shabby
in Scotland a potato is a tattie, and King Edward is a potato variety

explanation.surface: A Scot is asked how they regard a monarch who was hardly beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato variety; tattie or tatty is Scots for potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means shabby and cheap-looking; the Scottish spelling also names the potato.

clue.text: Not post to offer professor

parts.note: pre is the opposite of post, before rather than after
to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: Instead of mailing it, someone decides to hand it to the academic in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'professor' is not an academic but one who professes, claiming something, here falsely.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who professes a claim, such as to a throne, without right is a claimant of that kind.
